head: PlainApp: free Android app opens your phone's files in a PC browser
dek: PlainApp is a free, open-source Android app that lets a computer on the same Wi-Fi open your phone's photos, videos, music, contacts and folders in a web browser, with no account and nothing to install on the PC. Engadget tried it and found most of it works, though remote control didn't.
details: It needs Android 9 or newer and is on Google Play. Files move both ways, and it has a photo and video viewer, an image editor, a music player, screen mirroring, and can send text to the phone's clipboard or call a number. The first visit shows a browser warning because the app uses its own certificate. Engadget found Quick Share faster for moving photos and videos.
where: Android 9 or newer, free on Google Play; any computer with a browser on the same Wi-Fi
means: If you move files between your Android phone and a computer without a cable, PlainApp does it in a browser tab with no sign-up.
todo: Install PlainApp from Google Play, allow notification and file access, connect the PC to the same Wi-Fi, open the address the app shows, get past the certificate warning (Advanced, then Proceed), click Log in and allow it on the phone.
thumb_words: PLAINAPP: PHONE FILES IN A BROWSER
